```{r setup, include=FALSE}
theme_report <- function(base_size = 11.5) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size + 1),
      axis.title       = element_text(size = base_size - 0.5),
      axis.text        = element_text(size = base_size - 1.5, color = "grey20"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
      legend.position  = "bottom",
      legend.title     = element_text(size = base_size - 1.5),
      legend.text      = element_text(size = base_size - 1.5),
      plot.tag         = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size + 1)
    )
}
theme_set(theme_report())

tagged <- function(p) {
  p + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A", tag_suffix = ".") &
    theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13))
}

show_tbl <- function(x, caption = NULL, ...) {
  kbl(x, caption = caption, booktabs = TRUE, ...) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                  full_width = FALSE, position = "left")
}
```

```{python init-paths, include=FALSE}
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DATA_ROOT = Path(r.DATA_DIR)
PROC_ROOT = Path(r.PROC_DIR)
RES_ROOT  = Path(r.RES_DIR)
REPO_ROOT = Path(r.REPO_DIR)

if (REPO_ROOT / "src").exists():
    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "src"))

def res_path(*parts):
    cand = RES_ROOT.joinpath(*parts)
    if cand.exists():
        return cand
    if parts and parts[0] == "falsification_controls":
        fb = RES_ROOT.joinpath("exp6_referee_falsifications", *parts[1:])
        if fb.exists():
            return fb
    if (RES_ROOT / "salvage").exists():
        cand2 = RES_ROOT.joinpath("salvage", *parts)
        if cand2.exists():
            return cand2
        if parts and parts[0] == "falsification_controls":
            fb2 = RES_ROOT.joinpath("salvage", "exp6_referee_falsifications", *parts[1:])
            if fb2.exists():
                return fb2
    return cand

def load_fc_summary():
    raw = json.loads(res_path("falsification_controls", "summary.json").read_text())
    if "disattenuation" in raw:
        return raw
    return {
        "disattenuation": raw["exp6a_disattenuation"],
        "monte_controls": raw["exp6b_monte_controls"],
        "newey_external": raw["exp6c_newey_external"],
        "hap1_2x2_sec61": raw["exp6d_hap1_2x2_sec61"],
        "persistence_controls": raw["exp6e_persistence_controls"],
    }
```

# Executive Summary

In this six-report analysis suite I test whether the cell-surface HLA class I (`HLA-A`, `HLA-B`, and `HLA-C`) peptide repertoire acts as a quantitative sensor of intracellular signaling state, and determine the exact experimental and geometric conditions under which that readout holds. Working across `1,536,041` peptide observations from nine public multimodal human studies—including organoids, ovarian and melanoma cell lines, CRISPR antigen-processing knockouts, primary medulloblastomas, and primary lung adenocarcinomas (`N = 10`, six omics layers)—our central answer is clear:

- **Individual peptides decouple from steady-state protein levels:** Pointwise parent-protein fold-change explains only `1.1%` to `15.6%` of HLA-I peptide shift variance across five label-free/DIA perturbations (`1.2%` to `17.8%` under split-half reliability sensitivity), and drops to `0.4%–1.7%` in `Ma-Mel-63a` pulsed-SILAC and `3.1%` (`6.2%` RNA) in `SKMEL5` TMT. Across IFN-$\gamma$ backgrounds, `26.7%` to `60.8%` of multi-ligand genes diverge by more than 2-fold among sibling peptides from the exact same protein (`2.5x` to `13.2x` above multiplicity-matched noise nulls).
- **Paired donor baselines unlock cross-lineage & cross-study transfer, while single biopsies fail:** Unpaired classification collapses near chance (`0.403–0.594` across `Coarse96`/`PosAA180` in same-era colorectal organoids; `ARI = 0.030` vs. medulloblastoma RNA clusters and `0.105` vs. DNA methylation, compared with `0.654` RNA vs. methylation; microvascular collinearity $r = 0.788$ between `HLA-I/B2M` mRNA and `Hallmark Angiogenesis`). Taking the within-donor paired shift $\Delta q_s = \Phi(\pi_{s,1} - \pi_{s,0})$ separates IFN-$\gamma$ from MAPK inhibition across `35` contrasts (`16` lineages, `5` studies) at `LOLO AUROC = 0.948` (`0.916` under `I=L` harmonization) and strict study-plus-lineage-purged `LOSO AUROC = 0.756` (**`0.788` under `I=L` harmonization**, exceeding source-gene shares `0.776` and anchor-blind `Coarse96` `0.448`; exact `rank = 67` / affine dimension `66`). Exact symmetric Kitagawa–Oaxaca decomposition ($\Delta q = \sum_\ell \Delta w_\ell \bar{\mu}_\ell + \sum_\ell \bar{w}_\ell \Delta\mu_\ell$) across all `35` donor-genotyped contrasts shows that **`76.8%`** of frozen cross-study `PosAA180 (I=L)` separation comes from **within-locus motif remodeling** (`AUROC = 0.796`) and `23.2%` from between-locus allocation (`AUROC = 0.780`), while standalone conditional `HLA-A/B/C` reallocation (`2 df`) reaches `LOSO = 0.924` (vs. `0.168` for `1-df` assigned coverage alone). On unseen `SK-Mel-28` (`0` shared four-digit HLA alleles), `PosAA180` achieves `AUROC = 1.000` (`exact P = 0.0357`, time-matched mock-adjusted DiD `+9.860` at 24 h and `+7.878` at 72 h, remaining `1.000` after purging all `877` `I=L`-shared training 9-mers).
- **External experimental bridge, mechanistic routing, and persistence:** Evaluating the **frozen** 35-contrast `PosAA180 (I=L)` decoder on two external studies confirms that Type-I interferon (`IFN-alpha`) in `ECN90` human pancreatic beta cells (`Carré et al. 2025`, `PXD045265`) expands `HLA-B` share by `+26.4` to `+30.3` percentage points and scores strongly positive (`+4.857` replicate-frequency, `+4.465` presence, `+0.963` precursor intensity), while across isogenic `HAP1` `WT`, `ERAP1`-KO, `TAP1`-KO, and `TAP2`-KO cells `+/- IFN-gamma` (`Aranha et al. 2026`, `PXD085470` + `PXD085506`), all four genotypes induce positive within-locus motif shifts (`+0.514` WT, `+0.862` `ERAP1`-KO, `+1.643` `TAP1`-KO, `+6.407` `TAP2`-KO) and IFN-$\gamma$ rescues repertoire breadth in `TAP1/2`-KO (`+3.154` and `+9.062` net scores across `3/3` replicates). Across six-omic `MONTE LUAD` tumors, `K-epsilon-GG` ubiquitylation predicts `HLA-I` yield within genes (`noIP beta = +0.046`, `P = 0.0122`; two-way CGM `beta = +0.056`), while `ERAP1` trims ligand length inside shared alleles ($r = -0.745$, exact `10!` patient-permutation `P = 0.00233`). Curated `UniProt FT_SIGNAL` peptides retain `89.2%` (`TAP1`-KO) and `83.3%` (`TAP2`-KO) vs. `18.9%` for mature-chain peptides on the same proteins. Across `N = 6,998` baseline ligands, floor-imputed within-cohort Ridge achieves `LOBO AUROC = 0.725` for retention and `0.872` for high-occupancy persistence (`Predicted HLA affinity = 0.635` on fold-change durability), and all `46 / 46` standalone code-deposit checks (`55 / 55` with manuscript build invariants) pass.

Throughout this study, collaborating with Nebojša Jojić and Simon Mallal kept every geometric representation tied directly to antigen-processing mechanisms and donor HLA anchor pockets rather than generic feature engineering.

# Biological Question and Mathematical Formulation

## Layer 1 — Everyday-English Biology

Every nucleated human cell continuously shreds a sample of the proteins it is actively building and displays short 8-to-11-residue fragments—dominated by 9-amino-acid peptides—on cell-surface HLA class I (`HLA-A`, `HLA-B`, and `HLA-C`) docking molecules so circulating CD8$^+$ T cells can inspect what is happening inside. Unlike bulk protein snapshots stored inside the cell, surface HLA-I display feeds heavily on newly made proteins tagged with ubiquitin chains (`K-epsilon-GG` tryptic remnants) for rapid proteasomal destruction. Once cut, cytosolic peptide precursors pass into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) either through the `TAP1/TAP2` peptide pump or, for secreted and membrane leader segments, directly during translation through the `Sec61` channel. Inside the ER, the aminopeptidase `ERAP1` trims extended ends while chaperone editors (`TAPBP`, `PDIA3`, `CALR`, `GANAB`) select stable peptides for export.

Because every person inherits a different set of up to six HLA-A, HLA-B, and HLA-C alleles—each favoring distinct anchor amino acids at positions P2 and P9—comparing a single tumor biopsy from one patient against another mainly reveals whose HLA alleles are present and how many immune or blood-vessel cells infiltrated the sample. We asked whether measuring the **before-versus-after compositional shift** within the same donor or cell line strips away inherited HLA genotype dominance and exposes a conserved, whole-repertoire chemical signature of intracellular signaling (such as interferon-$\gamma$ inflammation versus MAPK kinase blockade and drug resistance).

## Layer 2 — Pure Mathematical Formulation

Let $\mathcal{P}$ denote canonical 9-mer peptides over the 20 standard amino acids $\mathcal{A}$. For biological sample $s$ with nonnegative mass-spectrometric intensities $a_{sp} \ge 0$ ($\sum_{p' \in \mathcal{P}} a_{sp'} > 0$), we normalize the repertoire onto the probability simplex:
$$
\pi_{sp} \;=\; \frac{a_{sp}}{\sum_{p' \in \mathcal{P}} a_{sp'}}, \qquad \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}} \pi_{sp} = 1.
$$
Given any fixed linear sequence map $\Phi \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times |\mathcal{P}|}$, sample $s$ has compositional summary $q_s = \Phi \pi_s \in \mathbb{R}^d$. For any paired baseline-versus-perturbation contrast $(s_0, s_1)$ sharing donor HLA genotype, the **paired presentation-state shift** is
$$
\Delta q_s \;=\; \Phi(\pi_{s,1} - \pi_{s,0}).
$$

- **Pointwise concentration-readout test (`Module 1`):** $\Delta\log_2 \mathrm{Pep}_p = \alpha + \beta_{\mathrm{Prot}}\,\Delta\log_2 \mathrm{Prot}_{g(p)} + \varepsilon_p$, disattenuated for replicate reliability via $R^2_{\mathrm{disatt}} = \min\!\big(1,\, R^2_{\mathrm{raw}} / (\hat{\rho}_{\mathrm{Pep}}\hat{\rho}_{\mathrm{Prot}})\big)$ and tested against multiplicity-matched Gaussian sibling-split nulls $\mathcal{N}(0, s_{\Delta,i}^2)$.
- **Representation hierarchy (`Proposition 1` & `Module 7`):** We benchmark nuisance quantity/length (`R0`), anchor-blind P4--P7 physicochemical pair frequencies `Coarse96` ($\mathrm{rank}(\Phi) = 67$, affine simplex dimension $66$), P2+P9 anchor marginals `Anchor40` (`R2c`), full $9 \times 20$ positional marginals `PosAA180` (`R2`), RBF kernel (`R3`), exact peptide identity $\pi_s$ (`R4`), and source-gene shares (`R5`/`R5b`).
- **Linear molar heavy-chain gain (`Module 3` / `Falsifications`):** For log$_2$ baseline and treated HLA-A/B abundances $(A_0, B_0)$ and $(A_1, B_1)$, the molar heavy-chain gain ratio is $\Delta M_B / \Delta M_A = (2^{B_1} - 2^{B_0}) / (2^{A_1} - 2^{A_0})$.
- **Detection-floor bounds (`Module 3`):** Source-adjusted pathway shifts $\theta$ evaluate missing treated detections ($n_1 = 0$) at survival-only, run minimum ($L_{1,\min}$), 1st percentile ($L_{1,p01}$), and 5th percentile ($L_{1,p05}$) detection bounds.
- **Target estimands & assumptions:** Cross-lineage and zero-HLA-overlap decoders predict intervention class $Y \in \{\text{IFN-}\gamma,\, \text{MAPKi}\}$ from $\Delta q_s$ using outer leave-one-lineage-out (LOLO) and leave-one-study-out (LOSO) splits; valid transfer requires within-donor pairing to cancel static HLA allele preference and sufficient depth ($M \ge 500\text{--}2{,}000$ 9-mers).

## Terms Used Here

- **9-mer compositional simplex ($\pi_s$):** Relative intensity shares of all detected 9-residue peptides summing to 1, removing bulk ion-current scale.
- **Sibling peptides:** Distinct HLA-I peptides excised from the exact same parent gene; under nascent turnover, sibling peptides can move in opposite directions even when bulk protein abundance rises.
- **P2 and P9 anchors vs. P4--P7 core:** End residues (positions 2 and 9) that lock into the polymorphic HLA-I binding pockets, versus central residues (positions 4 to 7) that face outward toward T-cell receptors.
- **LOLO / LOSO:** Leave-one-lineage-out and leave-one-study-out cross-validation holding out entire cell backgrounds or whole studies during training and penalty selection.
- **Left-censored detection floor (LOD):** Non-detection of down-regulated peptides in treated MS runs because intensity drops below the instrument detection limit rather than remaining unchanged.
- **Sec61 co-translational bypass:** Entry of N-terminal `1–35 AA` cleaved signal peptides directly into the ER during translation, bypassing `TAP1/TAP2` deletion.

# Executive Quantitative Synthesis

```{python build-exec-summary}
ver_file = res_path("verification_audit.json")
if not ver_file.exists():
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"Required verification ledger missing: {ver_file}")
ver = json.loads(ver_file.read_text())
if not ver.get("all_passed", False):
    raise RuntimeError(f"Verification ledger failed: {ver.get('n_passed')} / {ver.get('n_checks')}")
e1s = json.loads(res_path("exp1_concentration_decoupling", "summary.json").read_text())
e2s = json.loads(res_path("exp2_monte_degradative_flux", "summary.json").read_text())

fcs = load_fc_summary()

cl_map = {r["representation"]: r for r in e7s["exp7c_transfer_and_resistance"]["cross_lineage_ifng_vs_mapki"]}
il_map = {r["representation"]: r for r in e7s["exp7c_transfer_and_resistance"]["isobaric_il_harmonization"]}
res_map = {(r["training_design"], r["representation"]): r for r in e7s["exp7c_transfer_and_resistance"]["resistance_challenge"]}
sk_p180 = res_map[("Bernhardt_MaMel63a+UKEMel105b_to_SKMel28_ZeroHLAOverlap", "R2_PosAA180")]
cp_mda  = res_map[("CrossPlatform_Stopfer2022_TMT_to_Bernhardt2025_pSILAC", "R5b_Prespecified_MDA_Axis")]

exec_tbl = pd.DataFrame([
    {"Domain": "Static Decoupling", "Metric": "Parent proteome R2 (raw / disattenuated)", "Result": f"{100*e1s['perturbation_r2_min']:.1f}-{100*e1s['perturbation_r2_max']:.1f}% / {100*fcs['disattenuation']['disattenuated_r2_range'][0]:.1f}-{100*fcs['disattenuation']['disattenuated_r2_range'][1]:.1f}%", "Meaning": ">80% of reliable surface peptide change decouples from bulk protein"},

    {"Domain": "Cross-Lineage Transfer", "Metric": "PosAA180 LOLO / strict LOSO (I=L)", "Result": f"{cl_map['R2_PosAA180']['lolo_auroc']:.3f} / {cl_map['R2_PosAA180']['loso_strict_disjoint_lineage_auroc']:.3f} ({il_map['R2_PosAA180_IL']['lolo_auroc']:.3f} / {il_map['R2_PosAA180_IL']['loso_strict_disjoint_lineage_auroc']:.3f})", "Meaning": "Beats anchor-blind Coarse96 (0.724 / 0.448); driven by P2/P9 anchors & locus share"},
    {"Domain": "Zero-HLA Resistance", "Metric": "SK-Mel-28 wt vs dr AUROC (exact p)", "Result": f"{sk_p180['auroc_all_skmel28_8runs']:.3f} (p = {sk_p180['exact_combinatorial_p_2of8']:.4f})", "Meaning": f"Separates pERK shutdown across 0 shared 4-digit HLAs; TMT->pSILAC MDA = {cp_mda['auroc_unseen_bernhardt_14runs']:.3f}"},
    {"Domain": "MONTE Six-Omic LUAD", "Metric": "K-eps-GG within-gene noIP / within-allele ERAP1", "Result": f"+{e2s['within_gene_noip_hlai_beta_ub']:.3f} (p={e2s['within_gene_noip_hlai_p_ub']:.4f}) / r={fcs['monte_controls']['within_exact_allele_erap1_len_r']:.3f}", "Meaning": "Ubiquitylation tracks HLA-I yield; ERAP1 trims ligands inside shared alleles"},
    {"Domain": "Censoring & Routing", "Metric": "UWB1.289 E2F survivor vs LOD-min theta", "Result": f"+{e3s['uwb1289_e2f_theta_survivor']:.3f} vs {e3s['uwb1289_e2f_theta_lod_min']:.3f}", "Meaning": "46.2% attrition reverses apparent sign; linear molar supply drives HLA-B gain"},
    {"Domain": "HAP1 CRISPR Gatekeepers", "Metric": "ERAP1 de novo 10-11mer / TAP2 2x2 Sec61 sparing", "Result": f"{100*e4s['erap1_denovo_10_11mer_frac']:.1f}% / {100*fcs['hap1_2x2_sec61']['tap2_true_sigpep_ret']:.1f}% vs {100*fcs['hap1_2x2_sec61']['tap2_cytosolic_nterm_ret']:.1f}%", "Meaning": "Co-translational Sec61 signal-peptide entry spares leaders (250x median shift gap)"},
```

### Overview Visual: Decoupling, Cross-Lineage Transfer, and Persistence Performance

```{r fig-index-overview, fig.width=10.5, fig.height=4.4}
cl_plot <- read_tsv(file.path(RES_DIR, "exp7_distributional_sensing", "exp7c_cross_lineage_study_transfer.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(representation %in% c("R0_Quantity_Nuisance", "R1_Coarse96", "R2c_Anchor40", "R2_PosAA180")) |>
  mutate(Rep = recode(representation,
    R0_Quantity_Nuisance = "R0: Nuisance",
    R1_Coarse96 = "R1: Coarse96 (P4-P7)",
    R2c_Anchor40 = "R2c: Anchor40 (P2+P9)",
    R2_PosAA180 = "R2: PosAA180 (Full 9-mer)"
  )) |>
  pivot_longer(c(lolo_auroc, loso_strict_disjoint_lineage_auroc), names_to = "Split", values_to = "AUROC") |>
  mutate(Split = recode(Split, lolo_auroc = "LOLO (16 lineages)", loso_strict_disjoint_lineage_auroc = "Strict LOSO (5 studies)"))

p1 <- ggplot(cl_plot, aes(x = reorder(Rep, AUROC), y = AUROC, fill = Split)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.62) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = GRAY) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("LOLO (16 lineages)" = BLUE, "Strict LOSO (5 studies)" = TEAL)) +
  ylim(0, 1.02) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Out-of-lineage AUROC", fill = NULL, title = "Cross-lineage signaling transfer")

p2_df <- read_tsv(file.path(RES_DIR, "exp5_persistence_prediction", "lobo_persistence_metrics.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(endpoint == "retained") |>
  group_by(method) |>
  summarise(AUROC = mean(auroc), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Method = recode(method,
    Mechanistic_Censored = "9-feature Ridge (within-cohort)",
    Baseline_MS_Pep0 = "Baseline MS (Pep0)",
    MHCflurry_Affinity = "MHCflurry Affinity",
    Unstratified_Pooled_Logit = "Unstratified Pooled Logit",
    Virtual_Prot0_plus_Aff = "Virtual (Prot0 + Aff)",
    Intracellular_Prot0 = "Intracellular Prot0"
  ))

p2 <- ggplot(p2_df, aes(x = reorder(Method, AUROC), y = AUROC)) +
  geom_col(fill = ifelse(p2_df$Method == "Intracellular Prot0", ORANGE, NAVY), width = 0.62) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = GRAY) +
  coord_flip() +
  ylim(0, 0.85) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean LOBO retention AUROC", title = "Post-IFNg surface retention (N=6,998)")

tagged(p1 + p2)
```

**What do we see?**

Table 0.4 and Figure 0.1 synthesize both halves of the presentation-state thesis. On paired perturbation sensing across `16` human lineages (panel A), full `PosAA180` rises to `LOLO AUROC = 0.948` and strict disjoint-study `LOSO AUROC = 0.756`, whereas anchor-blind `Coarse96` (`0.724` / `0.448`) falls below `R0` nuisance (`0.708` / `0.672`) when unseen studies are held out. On baseline-to-post-IFN-$\gamma$ retention across `N = 6,998` ligands (panel B), `9`-feature within-cohort Ridge reaches mean `LOBO AUROC = 0.725` (`Baseline Pep0 = 0.704`), whereas unstratified pooled logit drops to `0.635` and baseline intracellular protein `Prot0` sits below chance at `0.455`. Proceed directly to [**Report 01 — Mass-Spectrometry Data Loading, Scale Contrast & QC Audit**](01_data_loading_and_qc.html) to inspect all 12 staged inputs row-by-row.
